messages:
sam (oncall): noticing a p99 jump on model-3-13b serving pool us-west-2-prod, started ~12:05 UTC. baseline ~120ms now ~270ms. any immediate suspects?

maria (eng-runtime): thanks — rolling up graphs now. did anything land in runtime in the last hour?

deploy-bot: new deploy: runtime-service v1.56.0 -> v1.57.0 to us-west-2 at 11:58 UTC by kira

sam (oncall): hmm deploy timing matches. also infra rolled CUDA driver 535.54 across the fleet ~11:50 UTC.

kira (infra): that driver rollout was staged; only on the G5p pools. Are model-3-13b instances on G5p?

maria (eng-runtime): yes, some of the dedicated pool is G5p. I'm pulling flamegraphs/profile traces from the slow pods. initial perf profile shows an uptick in kernel launch latency and some kernel selection fallbacks. snippet from perf trace: 
```
[11:59:12] cudaLaunch: aten_flash_attn_fwd_v2 - 1.8ms
[12:05:03] cudaLaunch: aten_flash_attn_fwd_v2 - 9.7ms (autoselect=triton_fallback)
[12:05:04] kv_cache::apply_prefix - increased wait 35ms
```

dave (eng-ml): autoselect switching to triton_fallback for the FlashAttention path would explain the token latency spike. Did the kernel selector heuristic change in v1.57?

maria (eng-runtime): v1.57 bumped the kernel autoselect to prefer newer Triton kernels when driver >=535 to exploit new kernels. apparently fallback paths are more expensive if batch shapes are small.

jin (eng-sre): is there evidence of noisy neighbor (other tenant saturating GPU)? nvidia-smi shows occasional high SM utilization but not constant. posting probe: 
```
$ nvidia-smi dmon -s u -c 5
# gpu sm mem enc dec mclk pwr temp
0 13 4 0 0 500 85 72
1 94 6 0 0 1200 240 81  
```

kira (infra): GPU1 looks saturated by another process. that could trigger different kernel choices if the runtime observes different SM occupancy.

sam (oncall): timeline: driver rollout -> runtime deploy -> latency jump. we need to triage whether driver-induced kernel behavior or noisy neighbor or runtime heuristic bug. fast triage steps?

maria (eng-runtime): quick repro: run a short harness with tiny batch (1-2) and sequence 512 on G5p driver 535.54 and compare kernels selected with old driver 530.x. I can spin a couple of containers to test.

dave (eng-ml): also try forcing disable of Triton path: env FLASHATTN_ENABLE_TRITON=0 or runtime flag --kernel-selector=legacy and see p99. If latency drops back we're isolating to selector heuristics.

maria (eng-runtime): running the harness now. prelim result: with triton enabled on 535 driver, observed frequent kernel fallback to 'triton_fallback' which has higher per-launch overhead at small batch sizes. With --kernel-selector=legacy p99 returns to ~130ms.

sam (oncall): good signal. do we have logs showing why autoselect picked fallback? maybe shape mismatch or dynamic tuning fail.

maria (eng-runtime): selector log snippet: 
```
[selector] candidate: triton_flash_kv_sm8x - attempt tunefail (cuCtxSynchronize err=700)
[selector] fallback -> aten_flash_attn_fwd_v2 (cuda_compat=ok)
[selector] policy: prefer_triton_if_driver>=535 && expected_batch>4
```

jin (eng-sre): err=700 is CUDA error 700 (unknown). Could be driver/hardware interaction. Also seeing intermittent 'cuMemAlloc' latency spikes in the same time window.

kira (infra): rolling back driver fleet-wide is heavy. can we hotfix runtime to revert the new autoselect policy and push to the affected pools?

maria (eng-runtime): yes we can patch v1.57 -> v1.57.1 with kernel-autoselect toggle defaulting to legacy for driver>=535. small canary now.

deploy-bot: deploy started: runtime-service v1.57.1 to us-west-2-canary - 12:30 UTC

dave (eng-ml): parallel test: KV cache behavior looked impacted because some requests waited for fallback kernels causing backlog and then the batching heuristic started to coalesce heterogeneous seq lengths and caused head-of-line blocking. That's why we saw kv_cache::apply_prefix wait increase.

sam (oncall): so root cause chain hypothesis: driver update + runtime autoselect -> selector tries new Triton kernels -> tuning/runtime errors (cuda err 700) -> fallback to slower kernels -> per-request latency increase -> batching heuristics coalesce different seq lengths -> KV prefix apply waits increase -> end-to-end p99 spike. plus noisy neighbor made selector pick different kernels due to occupancy.

maria (eng-runtime): can confirm canary v1.57.1 (legacy selector) reduced p99 to baseline after 10k samples. pushing to production after short soak.

deploy-bot: deploy success: runtime-service v1.57.1 rolled to us-west-2-prod - 12:56 UTC

jin (eng-sre): post-rollback stats: p50 stable, p99 back to ~125ms. no more kernel fallback logs. Monitoring will keep 48h watch.

kira (infra): follow-ups: we'll pause driver rollout to other pools until we've validated the Triton kernels with our workloads and maybe backport a compat test to the driver upgrade playbook.

maria (eng-runtime): action items: (1) add stricter autotune failure handling and circuit-breaker for selector. (2) instrument per-kernel selection counts in metrics (already adding a stat). (3) update batching heuristic: avoid merging sequences when fallback rate > 5% to reduce kv cache stalls. (4) add driver compatibility e2e in CI for small-batch shapes.

dave (eng-ml): add a small regression test with seq lengths 128/512/1024 and batch 1-4 to model onboarding. it caught these micro-behavior differences for us.

sam (oncall): thanks everyone. note in incidents channel with summary and link to logs. leaving monitoring alerts on until we see stable numbers for 48h. :white_check_mark:

maria (eng-runtime): adding detailed trace and selector logs to the incident ticket. I'll follow up w/ PR references for the hotfix + heuristics changes.

sam (oncall): great work. noise source PID 23456 on GPU1 was tenant-job-42; infra will throttle/evict if repeats.

kira (infra): flagged tenant-job-42 for noisy-neighbor mitigation and put driver rollout on hold for non-critical pools.

maria (eng-runtime): final note: disabling Triton by default for 535+ is temporary; we want the perf wins but need controlled rollout and better fallback observability.

sam (oncall): closing thread here, will reopen if anything pops. thanks all. :bow:
